questions: Do you experience a sensation that the environment is moving or bouncing when your eyes move?
Have these abnormal eye movements been present since childhood?
Did these eye movements begin suddenly within the last few days or weeks?
Do you have double vision?
Do you have dizziness, imbalance, weakness, numbness, difficulty speaking, or severe headache?
Are you taking anticonvulsants, sedatives, lithium, or other psychiatric medications?
Do the eye movements worsen when you look to either side?
Can you intentionally start and stop the abnormal eye movements?
Do the eye movements consist of rapid, back-and-forth horizontal movements?
Do they occur only when you try to make them happen or when you deliberately shift your gaze?
Have you had recent fever, viral illness, vaccination, or infection?
Have you had hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or a spinning sensation?
Do you have recurrent headaches, light sensitivity, or visual aura?
Have you ever had episodes of loss of consciousness, seizures, or confusion?
Have you had prior episodes of weakness, numbness, imbalance, or speech difficulty that resolved?
Do the abnormal eye movements occur during, immediately before, or immediately after your seizures?
Are your seizures characterized by brief staring spells with impaired awareness?
Do rapid blinking or upward jerking of the eyes occur when you close your eyes?
Are your seizures triggered by flashing lights or visual patterns?
Have you had sudden brief jerks of your arms, especially shortly after waking?
Have you had generalized convulsive seizures with stiffening and rhythmic jerking?
Do you have a family history of epilepsy or similar abnormal eye movements?
Have you had developmental delay, progressive memory or coordination problems, or cognitive decline?
Do you have difficulty walking, clumsiness, or trouble coordinating your hands?
Do you have involuntary jerks or tremors other than during the seizures?
Have the abnormal eye movements progressively worsened over time?
Have you had unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or an underlying cancer diagnosis?
Have you had a recent tick bite, diarrheal illness, or exposure to contaminated food or water?
Have you ever had liver disease, jaundice, psychiatric changes, or a tremor?
Have you noticed a brown ring around the colored part of either eye?
Did the generalized seizures begin before the abnormal eye movements?
orders: MRI of the brain and brainstem with and without gadolinium contrast, including thin-section imaging of the cerebellum and internal auditory canals.
Prolonged video-electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring with simultaneous video recording and eye-movement channels, including attempted capture of the abnormal eye movements and sleep.

Lumbar puncture with cerebrospinal-fluid cell count, protein, glucose, oligoclonal bands, IgG index, infectious PCR panel, and paired serum/CSF autoimmune encephalitis and paraneoplastic antibody panels, including anti-GAD65, NMDA-receptor, AMPA-receptor, GABA-B-receptor, LGI1, CASPR2, Hu, Ri, Yo, Ma2, and CRMP5 antibodies.
Genetic testing for progressive myoclonus epilepsy and cerebellar ataxia genes, including **KCNC1**, **SACS**, **STXBP1**, and common spinocerebellar ataxia repeat expansions.
served: CSF oligoclonal bands and IgG index
